recipes.title: Vietnamese mushroom pho, light
recipes.summary: A fragrant vegan pho with rice noodles, mushrooms and a deeply aromatic broth. Extra mushrooms and a modest noodle portion keep the bowl generous but light.

steps.instruction: Slice the shiitake mushrooms, mushrooms, ginger, spring onions and cilantro, then prepare the onion, garlic and lime.
Heat the sesame oil in a large pot and cook the onion, ginger and garlic until their cut surfaces are lightly browned.
Add the vegetable broth, soy sauce, star anise and cinnamon to the pot.
Simmer the broth gently until the star anise, cinnamon, onion and ginger have infused it with a warm aroma.
Add the shiitake mushrooms and mushrooms and simmer until tender.
Cook the rice noodles separately until tender but still slightly springy, then drain them.
Remove the onion, star anise and cinnamon from the broth and taste for balance.
Divide the rice noodles and mushrooms between bowls and ladle over the hot broth.
Finish each bowl with spring onions, cilantro and lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Store the broth and rice noodles separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the broth until boiling and add the noodles just before serving. Freeze the broth without the fresh toppings for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Vietnamese mushroom pho
recipes.summary: A warming vegan Vietnamese pho with tender rice noodles and two kinds of mushrooms. Star anise, cinnamon, ginger and charred onion give the broth its defining fragrance.

steps.instruction: Slice the shiitake mushrooms, mushrooms, ginger, spring onions and cilantro, then prepare the onion, garlic and lime.
Heat the sesame oil in a large pot and cook the onion, ginger and garlic until lightly charred at the edges.
Add the vegetable broth, soy sauce, star anise and cinnamon to the pot.
Simmer the broth gently until the star anise, cinnamon, onion and ginger have created a fragrant base.
Add the shiitake mushrooms and mushrooms and simmer until tender and savoury.
Cook the rice noodles separately until tender with a slight chew, then drain them.
Remove the onion, star anise and cinnamon from the broth.
Divide the rice noodles and mushrooms between bowls and ladle over the hot broth.
Finish each bowl with spring onions, cilantro and lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate broth and rice noodles separately for up to 3 days. Reheat the broth until steaming and warm the noodles in it briefly. Freeze the strained broth for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Vietnamese mushroom pho, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous vegan pho with extra rice noodles and mushrooms in a richly spiced Vietnamese broth. It is substantial enough for dinner while remaining fresh and aromatic.

steps.instruction: Slice the shiitake mushrooms, mushrooms, ginger, spring onions and cilantro, then prepare the onion, garlic and lime.
Heat the sesame oil in a large pot and cook the onion, ginger and garlic until well browned at the edges.
Add the vegetable broth, soy sauce, star anise and cinnamon to the pot.
Simmer the broth gently until the star anise, cinnamon, onion and ginger have deeply flavoured it.
Add the shiitake mushrooms and mushrooms and simmer until completely tender.
Cook the rice noodles separately until tender but not soft, then drain them thoroughly.
Remove the onion, star anise and cinnamon from the broth.
Divide the rice noodles and mushrooms between large bowls and ladle over the broth.
Finish each bowl generously with spring onions, cilantro and lime.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep the broth and rice noodles in separate containers for up to 3 days. Reheat only the portion required. The strained mushroom broth freezes well for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Kelewele, light
recipes.summary: Warm Ghanaian-style fried plantain seasoned with ginger, cayenne, paprika and cinnamon. The lighter version uses firm plantain and less oil while keeping the edges caramelised.

ingredients.name: plantain
ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut into bite-size pieces

steps.instruction: Peel the plantain and cut it into evenly sized bite-size pieces.
Mix the ginger, cayenne pepper, paprika, cinnamon and salt into a thick seasoning paste.
Coat the plantain thoroughly with the ginger and spice mixture.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the plantain until caramelised and golden on several sides, turning the pieces regularly.
Rest the kelewele briefly on absorbent paper before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Best served hot while the edges are caramelised. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat in a dry pan or hot oven. Freezing is not recommended because the plantain softens.

recipes.title: Kelewele
recipes.summary: Sweet ripe plantain fried with ginger, cayenne, paprika and cinnamon until deeply golden. This Ghanaian snack is fragrant, spicy and crisp around the edges.

ingredients.name: plantain
ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut into bite-size pieces

steps.instruction: Peel the plantain and cut it into evenly sized bite-size pieces.
Mix the ginger, cayenne pepper, paprika, cinnamon and salt into a thick seasoning paste.
Coat the plantain thoroughly with the ginger and spice mixture.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wide frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the plantain until deeply golden, sticky and caramelised around the edges.
Rest the kelewele briefly on absorbent paper before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Kelewele is at its best immediately after frying. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat in a hot dry pan or oven. Do not freeze.

recipes.title: Kelewele, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous platter of Ghanaian spiced plantain with a deeply caramelised crust. Extra plantain, ginger and warm spices make it an abundant snack for sharing.

ingredients.name: plantain
ingredients.preparation: peeled and cut into bite-size pieces

steps.instruction: Peel the plantain and cut it into evenly sized bite-size pieces.
Mix the ginger, cayenne pepper, paprika, cinnamon and salt into a thick seasoning paste.
Coat the plantain thoroughly with the ginger and spice mixture.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the plantain in batches until deeply browned and caramelised on every side.
Rest the kelewele briefly on absorbent paper before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Serve hot for the best texture. Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat in a hot oven or dry frying pan. The cooked plantain is not suitable for freezing.

recipes.title: Cured pork and egg congee, light
recipes.summary: A silky Chinese breakfast porridge with cured pork, ginger and softly cooked eggs. Extra broth keeps the bowl generous while the rice and pork remain restrained.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Slice the cured pork, ginger and spring onions into their prepared sizes.
Bring the chicken broth to a steady simmer in a deep saucepan.
Add the white rice, cured pork and ginger and simmer until the rice breaks down into a silky porridge.
Crack the eggs into the congee and cook until the whites are set but the yolks remain tender.
Stir the soy sauce and sesame oil through the congee.
Divide the congee between bowls and finish with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 2 days. Reheat gently with extra chicken broth because congee thickens considerably as it cools. Cook fresh eggs when reheating leftovers for the best texture.

recipes.title: Cured pork and egg congee
recipes.summary: Comforting Chinese congee simmered until creamy with cured pork and ginger, then finished with eggs, soy sauce and sesame oil. It is savoury, warming and ideal for breakfast.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Slice the cured pork, ginger and spring onions into their prepared sizes.
Bring the chicken broth to a steady simmer in a deep saucepan.
Add the white rice, cured pork and ginger and simmer until the grains collapse into a creamy congee.
Crack the eggs into the congee and cook until the whites are set and the yolks are softly cooked.
Stir the soy sauce and sesame oil through the hot congee.
Divide the congee between bowls and scatter over the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 2 days. Reheat with additional chicken broth until steaming and loose enough to spoon. The eggs are best cooked fresh rather than stored in the porridge.

recipes.title: Cured pork and egg congee, hearty
recipes.summary: A substantial bowl of Chinese congee with extra rice, cured pork and two eggs per person. Ginger, soy sauce and sesame oil give the rich porridge a warm savoury finish.

steps.instruction: Rinse the white rice under cold water until the water runs mostly clear.
Slice the cured pork, ginger and spring onions into their prepared sizes.
Bring the chicken broth to a steady simmer in a large, deep saucepan.
Add the white rice, cured pork and ginger and simmer until the larger amount of rice becomes thick and creamy.
Crack the eggs into the congee and cook until the whites are set and the yolks reach your preferred consistency.
Stir the soy sauce and sesame oil evenly through the congee.
Divide the congee between large bowls and finish with the spring onions.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 2 days and loosen with chicken broth during reheating. Heat until steaming throughout. Freshly cooked eggs give a better result than reheated eggs.

recipes.title: Provençal baked cod, light
recipes.summary: Cod baked over potatoes and colourful vegetables in a garlicky tomato, olive and thyme sauce. Extra vegetables and less oil keep this Mediterranean lunch fresh and light.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Slice the potato, zucchini, bell pepper and onion and chop the garlic.
Simmer the potato slices in water until just beginning to soften, then drain them.
Heat half the olive oil in a wide pan and cook the onion and bell pepper until slightly softened.
Stir in the garlic, tomatoes, canned, tomato paste, green olives and thyme.
Arrange the potato and zucchini in a baking dish, spoon over the tomato mixture and bake until the vegetables are nearly tender.
Place the cod over the vegetables, brush with the remaining olive oil and bake until the cod flakes easily.
Finish the Provençal baked cod with the lemon juice before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 2 days and reheat covered until the cod is hot. The dish is best fresh because reheated cod can become firm. Freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Provençal baked cod
recipes.summary: Flaky cod baked with potatoes, zucchini, peppers, tomatoes, olives and thyme. The garlicky Provençal sauce turns simple ingredients into a colourful Mediterranean lunch.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.

Simmer the potato slices in water until just beginning to soften, then drain them.
Heat half the olive oil in a wide pan and cook the onion and bell pepper until softened at the edges.
Stir in the garlic, tomatoes, canned, tomato paste, green olives and thyme.
Arrange the potato and zucchini in a baking dish, spoon over the tomato mixture and bake until almost tender.
Place the cod over the vegetables, brush with the remaining olive oil and bake until the cod flakes easily.
Finish the Provençal baked cod with the lemon juice before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Keep refrigerated for up to 2 days and reheat covered to protect the cod from drying out. The finished dish does not freeze particularly well.

recipes.title: Provençal baked cod, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous tray of cod, potatoes and Mediterranean vegetables baked in a rich tomato, olive and thyme sauce. It makes a substantial French lunch for four.

steps.instruction: Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Slice the potato, zucchini, bell pepper and onion and chop the garlic.
Simmer the potato slices in water until just beginning to soften, then drain them.
Heat half the olive oil in a wide pan and cook the onion and bell pepper until slightly softened.
Stir in the garlic, tomatoes, canned, tomato paste, green olives and thyme.
Arrange the potato and zucchini in a deep baking dish, spoon over the tomato mixture and bake until nearly tender.
Place the cod over the vegetables, brush with the remaining olive oil and bake until the thick fillets flake easily.
Finish the Provençal baked cod with the lemon juice before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and reheat covered until steaming. The cod is most tender when freshly baked, so freezing is not recommended.

recipes.title: Greek fasolakia, light
recipes.summary: Greek green beans and potatoes slowly braised in tomato, olive oil and dill. Extra green beans and less potato keep this dairy-free dinner light but comforting.

steps.instruction: Trim the green beans and cut the potato, onion and garlic into their prepared sizes.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Add the tomatoes, canned, vegetable broth, green beans and potato to the pot.
Cover and simmer the fasolakia gently until the green beans and potato are completely tender.
Uncover the pot and simmer until the tomato sauce thickens around the vegetables.
Stir the dill weed through the hot fasolakia.
Finish the dish with the lemon juice before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Fasolakia keeps well for up to 4 days and is good warm or at room temperature. Reheat gently with a splash of vegetable broth. Freeze for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Greek fasolakia
recipes.summary: Traditional-style Greek green beans and potatoes braised slowly with tomatoes, garlic, dill and olive oil. The vegetables become tender and absorb the rich Mediterranean sauce.

steps.instruction: Trim the green beans and cut the potato, onion and garlic into their prepared sizes.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pot and cook the onion until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir until fragrant and lightly caramelised.
Add the tomatoes, canned, vegetable broth, green beans and potato to the pot.
Cover and simmer the fasolakia gently until the green beans and potato are very tender.
Uncover the pot and simmer until the tomato sauce becomes rich and spoonable.
Stir the dill weed through the cooked vegetables.
Finish the fasolakia with the lemon juice before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Refrigerate for up to 4 days and serve warm or at room temperature. Reheat gently with a little vegetable broth. Freeze in portions for up to 2 months.

recipes.title: Greek fasolakia, hearty
recipes.summary: A generous pot of Greek green beans and potatoes braised until tender in a rich tomato and olive oil sauce. Dill and lemon keep the substantial dairy-free dinner fresh.

steps.instruction: Trim the green beans and cut the potato, onion and garlic into their prepared sizes.
Heat the olive oil in a large pot and cook the onion until completely soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir until fragrant and slightly darkened.
Add the tomatoes, canned, vegetable broth, green beans and potato to the pot.
Cover and simmer the fasolakia gently until the larger amount of green beans and potato is completely tender.
Uncover the pot and simmer until the tomato sauce is thick and glossy.
Stir the dill weed evenly through the fasolakia.
Finish the dish with the lemon juice before serving.

recipes.storageNotes: Keeps for up to 4 days in the refrigerator and often tastes better the next day. Reheat gently with vegetable broth if needed. Freeze for up to 2 months.
